event.title: A citizen asks Sonah about the presidential term
event.description: Question received during an election period. The only indexed text is the 1996 Constitution: its article 6 was amended by Law No. 2008-1 of 14 April 2008.

responses.message:
The Constitution states that the President **“est rééligible”** – he may run for another term, and the text does not set a numerical limit on how many times he can be re‑elected[3].  

**Explanation**  
- The original 1996 Constitution limited the President to one renewal, but that provision was removed by the amendment of 2008 (and confirmed by the 2026 amendment).  
- The current wording simply allows re‑election without specifying a maximum number of terms.

**What you can do**  
- If you are interested in the exact legal interpretation or any future reforms, you can consult the Ministry of Justice or the Constitutional Council for any updates or proposed amendments.

citations.title: Loi constitutionnelle n° 2026/002
citations.excerpt: (nouveau) (1) Le Président de la République est élu au suffrage universel direct, égal et secret, a la majorité des suffrages exprimés. (2) Le Président de la République est élu pour un mandat de sept (07) ans. Il est rééligible. (3) L'élection a lieu vingt (20) jours au moins et cinquante (50) jours au plus avant…
